tb21_profile.skill: Classical CV on frame sequences: background/motion differencing, thresholding and centroid/blob tracking to localise a discrete temporal event (takeoff/landing frame) robustly enough to generalise from one example video to hidden ones
tb21_profile.domain: Python + OpenCV(cv2)/numpy video analysis, MP4 decoding, TOML output; monocular kinematics of a human subject
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec: write a standalone script that emits an exact-schema output file, developed against one sample and graded on a hidden corpus

TMax-15K.reason: Write one mp4-analysis script, develop on a single sample video, graded on hidden corpus; derive per-frame pixel time-series and decide an event.
Per-frame OpenCV thresholding plus centroid of the moving object, scored against hidden ground truth; the exact tracking loop this task needs.
Tracks a blob centroid frame-by-frame from mp4 and must reject non-physical jumps; same noisy-trajectory reasoning as detecting takeoff.
Separates static background from the moving projectile then takes per-frame centroids; background subtraction is the crux technique here too.
Detects motion-event frame numbers from a surveillance video by inter-frame difference and a threshold; same event-frame output as takeoff/land.
Extract frame-by-frame object position from mp4 with cv2, then infer hidden dynamics; same pixel-to-kinematics extraction on a fixed camera.
Locate the falling mass's vertical centre in every frame and turn positions into kinematics; same monocular fixed-camera geometry reasoning.
Brightest-spot detection per frame to reconstruct a trajectory, then fit; the video half matches, the C++ server half does not.
Parses mp4 frame by frame for a coloured object's centroid, then smooths and segments the trajectory into discrete states.
Finds the frame index maximising mean absolute difference with the next frame; frame-differencing to locate an event is the core heuristic.

Pixel decoder swaps rows/columns and bits metadata; decoding frame buffers with correct geometry is the same failure class.
Decoding encapsulated multi-frame pixel data fails on fragment boundaries; multi-frame container handling, near-neighbour of mp4 decode.
BlendTransform over a large numpy image array; same CV transforms package, but the bug is in string formatting.
Colour generator over a numpy/PIL image with mismatched sizes; per-pixel array indexing and resizing discipline.
MP4 chunked upload fails; touches mp4 files but the skill is HTTP chunking, not frame content.
PageImage cropping produces wrong rendered dimensions; bounding-box to raster coordinate arithmetic.
TOML load/parse correctness; the TB2.1 deliverable is a TOML file with exact field names, so format fluency helps marginally.
Reading and writing TOML files after a library switch; only the output-format half of the TB2.1 task overlaps.

Spike-sorting analyzer selection over detected events; adjacent event-extraction-from-signal ecosystem, bug itself is plumbing.

final_top10.reason: Write one mp4-analysis script from a single dev video, graded on a hidden corpus; per-frame pixel time-series into a discrete decision.
Per-frame thresholding plus centroid tracking with OpenCV, scored against hidden ground-truth trajectories.
Centroid tracking of a blob through an mp4 plus rejection of non-physical jumps; noisy-trajectory judgement transfers directly.
Separates static background from the moving object then centroids each frame; background subtraction is the crux technique here too.
Emits the frame numbers where motion events occur, from inter-frame differences against a threshold.
Frame-by-frame position extraction from mp4 on a fixed camera with known scale, then inference of hidden dynamics.
Finds the object's vertical centre in every frame and converts pixel positions to physical kinematics; same monocular setup.
Brightest-spot per-frame localisation reconstructing a trajectory then fitting it; only the video stage transfers.
Per-frame colour-blob centroid extraction from mp4 followed by smoothing and segmentation of the trajectory.

notes: TMax dominates honestly: it is the only corpus with real cv2/ffmpeg frame-analysis tasks, so final_top10 is all TMax. Recursive-Task-Synthesis has essentially zero computer vision - searches for cv2/opencv/video/frame/pixel returned only env-setup chores (PyPEER, sds-mnist, GraphicsMagick builds); its ranks 5-10 are filler and should be treated as such. TerminalWorld is nearly as thin (tw_588262 YOLOv4/OpenCV is the only genuine CV entry). In SWE-Smith the fvcore transforms and pydicom pixel-decoder families are the only defensible CV picks; the TOML entries are included because the TB2.1 deliverable is a TOML file, but they teach nothing about the video half. The lexical shortlist was badly polluted for this task: TMax's top-ranked hits (task_000793, task_003268, task_002592, task_005184) all merely mention mp4 files while actually being crash-triage, pcap-forensics or red-square-artifact scans - none involve motion reasoning, so I demoted all of them.
